headline: High-risk filesystem and shell overlap: Replit Agent can write and modify git state while AutoGPT can execute shell and access the filesystem, creating dangerous interaction and leakage pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can read and act on filesystem content via its filesystem surface, while B can write Repl workspace files and modify git state. That shared file bridge makes prompt injection plausible if B writes attacker-controlled text that A later ingests as trusted instructions. No stronger shared channel is documented, so medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF B writes instructions or markdown into a file that A later reads as task context, injection is possible.
IF the pair is connected through a shared workspace or copied files, A may treat B-authored content as authoritative.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories or containers.
Require A to ignore instructions found in files unless explicitly user-authored.
Add a manual review step before A consumes any B-generated file.
Use read-only mounts for files passed from B to A.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all inter-agent file handoffs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B explicitly touches secrets and deployment configuration and has broad network egress; A has filesystem and shell access. If they share any workspace or file handoff, B can expose sensitive material and A can further process it, while B can transmit contents externally. The profiles do not show a protective isolation boundary, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF secrets or deployment files are present in the shared workspace, B can read them and send them over the network.
IF A receives those files from B, A can further expose them through shell commands or generated outputs.
mitigations: Remove secrets from any shared directory before running either agent.
Use separate workspaces with no shared filesystem.
Disable network egress for B during sensitive tasks.
Store secrets only in a manager not mounted into the workspace.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on files and egress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, and B can write the filesystem and modify git state while A can spawn subprocesses and access the filesystem. In a shared repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide and corrupt state. Because no locking or coordination primitive is documented, the interaction is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same repository or directory, simultaneous writes can conflict.
IF B commits or rewrites git state while A is running shell commands, repository corruption or lost work can occur.
mitigations: Run the agents in separate repositories or branches.
Serialize all write operations with a human gate.
Pause one agent while the other is modifying git state.
Use file locks around shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add an orchestrator-level mutex for workspace mutations.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can generate shell-driven outputs from filesystem content, and B can act inside a Repl with user checkpoints. If B consumes A's output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect code or deployment changes. The profiles do not prove automatic trust, so medium fits the documented pathway.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated text or commands without independent verification, mistakes can propagate into code or deployment changes.
IF A's filesystem-derived output is copied into B's task context, B may act on stale or incorrect facts.
mitigations: Require B to verify A outputs against source files before acting.
Add a checklist for any code or deployment change derived from A.
Keep A outputs as suggestions only, not direct commands.
Review diffs before B writes or commits them.
requires-engineering: add automated validation between A and B.

E_compliance.rationale: B touches secrets and deployment configuration and is cloud-hosted in Replit-managed infrastructure, while A is an open-source agent with filesystem and shell access. If regulated data is placed into B's workspace, residency and retention obligations may differ from A's local/open-source handling. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in B's Repl workspace, its cloud handling may differ from A's local handling.
IF the same sensitive dataset is processed by both agents, retention or residency mismatches can arise.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B's workspace.
Use synthetic or redacted data for shared tasks.
Confirm retention settings before uploading files to B.
Document which agent may handle which data class.
requires-engineering: obtain formal compliance mapping for both agents.
